title: Conditional κ = 0.00389846 with a fully charged 25-bit Gaussian installation
body:
## Conditional signed bound

**κ = 0.00389846** with ordinary heights (8192, 38102, 604362) and Gaussian height 18845936. This leaves **0.00000154** to 0.0039 and gains **0.000000245716808** over ToikY’s #8072. The price for the gain is explicit: complete recurring log₂ C rises from 318292011 to **4354317571**. The first terminal header is 2^19497094 + 2; entry costs 8744 conversion bits. The 25-bit Gaussian height enlarges the domain of the installer proof. The source-native words and their signed finite charges are retained.

The fixed serial construction generates 2,407,819 records and builds the actual 18,845,937-bit terminal carrier. An additional allowance of 2^40 actions covers the two carrier creations and profile records, including a computed carrier/scalar charge of 137556398080. Each stored κ and η numerator and denominator and each positive stop denominator is bounded by 128 bits. The actual profiles use at most 60 bits. Six malformed scalar controls were rejected, and the final charged setup command exited zero in 28.79 seconds. Recomputing the storage, lookup and arithmetic bounds keeps the fixed serial setup below 2^228.

## Source, prior work and hypotheses

[ToikY’s #8072](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8072) is pinned at `75f7e1c44f48c43983016bcf8878c4d9e5e87c62`. [#8078](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8078) at `b72d3fa097d2521939f6b8536029da674648d863` supplies the two lower budget points. #8076 improves a fixed-budget ordinary tariff. Floration’s overlapping [#8080](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8080), head `9127fc7eacf7d4e037efdf179deb54888a48665b`, reports 0.003898224460300 by changing the ordinary opening floor. Ali Romman supplied the #8057 signed supplier and #8055 setup argument; SYLforge supplied #8052’s K7 word. Notices are preserved. We refine the task to a larger positive-carrier parameter and its charged setup. The historical preflight parent is `0618e75a22cec54d1651394ef83d088551b7f026`.

The five inherited all-size premises concern signed native action, owned erasure and restoration, chronological mixed compilation, fixed-alphabet movement and precision, and analytic recovery. This is submitted for scientific review. Clear1nsight used OpenAI Codex Astra and Terra for construction, proof, auditing and packaging.

## Executed verification

On POSIX with Git and CPython 3.12, all eight registered commands passed individually with recorded exit code zero. They cover exact signed price, calendar and cutoff, both raw native widths, true exterior returns, nonzero nested transfers, signed products with restored operands, serial installer accounting, and source-blob checks. Reproduce the registered suite with `python3.12 -IB scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-expanded-budget-25bit`.

The terminal upper cutoff was checked by tracing the authenticated opening with symbolic powers and proving the exact integer floor inequalities. The same arguments agreed with literal arithmetic at heights 1024 and 2048. The product mode executed a finite entry coefficient fixture and constructed the high terminal supplier. The largest local resident set was 1,339,072 KiB during nested return. The final registration redistributes timeouts within 1,200 seconds. A production-dimensional multiplication, new WASI trace and independent human approval are outside the evidence.

## Open next question

The current Gaussian trial is 17145637307/2^42. The fixed-word funding certificate in [#8077](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8077) rules out reaching 0.0039 by height and positive rescaling alone. Which paid port can be physically removed or which independently owned target can be added while preserving every affected reader and returned operand?
